Class DeploymentPlan

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.optimizer.wizard.model.DeploymentPlan
public class DeploymentPlan extends Object
A complete deployment plan generated by the Deployment Wizard. Contains all planned Cloud Routers, provider connections, backbone links, routing protocols, and aggregated pricing. Supports review via toMarkdown(), dry-run validation via dryRun(), and full execution via execute().

    • dryRun

      public DeploymentPlan dryRun()
      Re-runs the layered plan-time validation and returns a new plan with the refreshed status.

      This is the same validation the wizard runs when it builds the plan: Layer 1 structural + catalog checks, Layer 2 live Cloud Router dry-run (POST /routers?dryRun=true), and Layer 3 connection endpoint dispatch — a connection whose A-side Cloud Router does not exist yet is recorded as deferred (its live endpoint dry-run runs at provisioning, and needs your authorization keys) rather than sent a doomed endpoint-less dry-run, while a connection with a pre-existing endpoint is dry-run for real. Nothing is provisioned: the router dry-run creates nothing, and to-be-created connections are never posted here.

      A live step that cannot be attempted — an offline / bare-stub run, or a live dry-run that the API answers with a non-rejection failure (403 not entitled, 429 throttled, 5xx, or a transport/timeout error) — is recorded as a skipped validation with a reason, never folded into the errors that invalidate the plan. Only a genuine rejection of a well-formed request (a 4xx validation rejection) is an error.

      Returns:
      a new DeploymentPlan with refreshed validity, deferred validations, skipped validations, and the required customer inputs

    • execute

      public DeploymentOutcome execute()
      Executes the deployment plan with no extra customer inputs — for a backbone-only plan, or a plan whose provider connections already carry their own authorization keys. Equivalent to execute(ExecutionInputs.none()): a provider connection that still needs a cloud authorization key fails fast (nothing is provisioned) naming the key to gather.
      Returns:
      the execution outcome with all provisioned resources and any errors

    • execute

      public DeploymentOutcome execute(ExecutionInputs inputs)
      Executes the deployment plan, creating all resources in the correct order: Cloud Routers, then provider connections, then backbone links, then routing protocols.

      Execution-time connection pre-flight (Layer 3a). A provider connection's live endpoint dry-run cannot run at plan time because its A-side Cloud Router does not exist yet; it runs here, at the only point it is possible. For each connection, once its A-side FCR is provisioned and its real uuid is known, a full connection body — real A-side uuid, Z-side service profile + seller region + the customer's authorization key, DOT1Q VLAN — is dry-run against the live API; only if the dry-run passes is the connection created for real. A dry-run rejection of a well-formed request (a 4xx validation rejection, e.g. HTTP 400/409) aborts the run and rolls back everything already provisioned (LIFO), so a broken plan never leaves billable Cloud Routers stranded.

      Pre-flight infeasibility never silently aborts. When the pre-flight dry-run cannot be attempted — an infeasibility rather than a rejection: 401/403 (not entitled), 429 (throttled), 5xx (server-side), or a transport/timeout error, classified by PlanValidator.classifyLiveFailure(Throwable) — the run does not abort. It records a recoverable warning that the pre-flight could not run and proceeds to the real create, which surfaces any genuine error itself. Only a true rejection aborts and rolls back. The fail-fast on a missing cloud authorization key (below) is unchanged.

      Required customer inputs. The cloud authorization keys — which a brand-new customer gathers from each cloud console — are supplied via inputs (keyed by connection name), or carried on the plan itself for a lens-3b plan. Before anything is provisioned, execution fails fast if any provider connection that needs a key is missing one, naming the connection and the exact key (ConnectionInputRequirement).

      Operational errors (a Cloud Router that does not reach PROVISIONED within the timeout, a missing upstream dependency) are captured in the outcome rather than thrown, allowing a partial deployment to be inspected and rolled back by the caller.

      An invalid plan never executes. A plan whose validation found hard errors (isValid() == false) is refused up front with an IllegalStateException listing every recorded error — executing it would provision billable resources and then fail downstream on the very defects validation already named. Fix the errors and re-plan (or dryRun() again) before executing.

      Parameters:
      inputs - the per-connection authorization keys, VLAN tags and Azure peering types the customer supplies; null is treated as ExecutionInputs.none()
      Returns:
      the execution outcome with all provisioned resources and any errors
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the plan is not valid — the message lists the validation errors to fix before re-planning

    • rollback

      public List<ProvisioningError> rollback(DeploymentOutcome outcome)
      Best-effort teardown of the resources provisioned by a prior execute(): deletes the connections (and backbone links), then the Cloud Routers, in reverse dependency order. Routing protocols are removed with their parent connection. Use this to clean up a partially-failed deployment rather than leaving orphaned, billable resources behind.
      Parameters:
      outcome - the outcome returned by execute()
      Returns:
      the deletions that failed (empty when the rollback was clean)
